page: Microsoft Azure D2s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, engineered for standard enterprise workloads requiring balanced system resources. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on the x86_64 architecture with a clock speed of up to 4.2 GHz. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 8.0 GB of memory, representing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI) are supported.

Hardware configurations for the D2s_v6 omit bundled local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached Premium Storage capabilities for persistent data. Network provisioning includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated Azure networking resources for external ingress. In benchmark testing, single-core processing showed balanced metrics, highlighted by strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.33 GB/sec and average stress-ng single-core execution (1940.78). However, multi-core throughput and memory subsystems demonstrate lower relative performance, with multi-core stress-ng yielding 1991.89 and large-block uncached read and write bandwidth reaching 20.8 GB/sec and 14.3 GB/sec, respectively.

Given its two-vCPU footprint and limited uncached memory throughput, the D2s_v6 presents a cost-efficient entry point for low-concurrency services. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, development environments, and small-scale caching layers that do not demand extensive parallel compute or local disk IOPS.

Sourced from a single physical core using two threads, the instance features hardware-accelerated instructions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX.
